title: Word order with onko with plural owners
summary: Build plural-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.
objectives: Build plural-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Build plural-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.
Put onko first, meillä, teillä, and heillä immediately after it, and the basic singular noun last. This lesson practises that order.
keyPoints: Build plural-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.

steps: Put Onko first to turn the possession pattern into a yes/no question.
Put meillä next. meillä means “we as the owner”.
Put koira (“dog”) last: Onko + owner + thing. Onko already contains on; do not add another on.
Put Onko first to turn the possession pattern into a yes/no question.
Put teillä next. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Put kirja (“book”) last: Onko + owner + thing. Onko already contains on; do not add another on.
Put Onko first to turn the possession pattern into a yes/no question.
Put heillä next. heillä means “they as the owner”.
Put kissa (“cat”) last: Onko + owner + thing. Onko already contains on; do not add another on.
Put Onko first to turn the possession pattern into a yes/no question.
Put teillä next. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Put tyyny (“pillow”) last: Onko + owner + thing. Onko already contains on; do not add another on.

commonMistakes: Reordering the words does not change fixed onko into a verb agreeing with the owner.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “Do they have a ball?” Put the owner immediately after the question word. Use heillä (“they as the owner”) and pallo (“a ball”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Follow the pattern: onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.formation: On + the yes/no question ending -ko = onko. It stays the same with every possessor.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
pallo stays in its basic singular form: one ball.
